summary.text: Harriet Hageman is Wyoming's at-large U.S. Representative, running for the state's open U.S. Senate seat in 2026. A Wyoming attorney for more than three decades, she was elected to the House in 2022 after defeating incumbent Liz Cheney in the Republican primary. She chairs a House Natural Resources subcommittee and serves on the Judiciary Committee.

paragraphs.text: Born in Douglas, Wyoming, in 1962. According to her House office, she grew up on a ranch and attended Casper College on a livestock judging scholarship.
Earned a bachelor's degree in business administration (1986) and a law degree (1989) from the University of Wyoming.

Worked as a law clerk for federal appeals judge James E. Barrett, as a lawyer, and as an adjunct professor. Her House biography says she was a litigator for 34 years, admitted to practice before the U.S. Supreme Court.
Co-founded the Wyoming Conservation Alliance and, according to Ballotpedia, was one of the chief litigators opposing the 2001 Roadless Rule.
Ran for Governor of Wyoming in the 2018 Republican primary, finishing third with 21.5% behind Mark Gordon and Foster Friess.
Won the 2022 Republican primary for Wyoming's at-large House seat, defeating incumbent Liz Cheney, and won the general election; re-elected in 2024.

In the 119th Congress, chairs the House Natural Resources Subcommittee on Water, Wildlife, and Fisheries and also serves on its Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee, on the Judiciary Committee, and as Co-Chair of the Congressional Coal Caucus.
Won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary for U.S. Senate, defeating Samuel Mead and three others, for the seat Sen. Cynthia Lummis is leaving.
